- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–3% per period until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–2 periods ahead to align with sentiment trend.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations, model tends to lag; forecast should be slightly ahead of true outcome by 1–2 periods in such cases.
